summary.whatChanges: The spy package now caches a bound reference to `Set.prototype.add` for its internal dirty-mock-state tracking instead of calling the method dynamically. This lets users spy on or mock `Set.prototype.add` without interfering with Vitest's internal mock bookkeeping. Tests cover spying on `Set.prototype.add` and calling mocked prototype methods while that spy is active.
behaviorChanges: `vi.spyOn(Set.prototype, 'add')` no longer records Vitest's own internal calls, so the spy only sees calls made by user code
Mock invocations no longer route through a user-replaceable `Set.prototype.add`, avoiding recursion/pollution when that method is spied on
Mocked prototype methods still register calls correctly while a `Set.prototype.add` spy is installed
`mockClear`, `vi.clearAllMocks` and `vi.resetAllMocks` behave as expected for a `Set.prototype.add` spy
risks: The bound reference is captured at module load; any earlier patching of `Set.prototype.add` in the environment would be baked into internal bookkeeping permanently
Only `add` is hardened — other built-in methods used internally (e.g. `Set.prototype.delete`, `WeakRef`, `FinalizationRegistry`) remain vulnerable to the same class of interference
